existingTemporalCaution.before: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
existingTemporalCaution.sourceChinese: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
existingTemporalCaution.reason: And now misleadingly suggests a death contemporaneous with the later correspondence. The passage recalls the Su Jun crisis; the linked annal continuation places the empress dowager’s death in Xianhe 3. Since supplied Chinese itself reads 至今, preserve the textual difficulty explicitly rather than silently emending Chinese or extracting a fresh 340-341 death event. No exact replacement is imposed for this unresolved textual issue.

proposals.before: Had the altars not been numinous and heaven not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
proposals.after: Had the altars not been numinous and men and spirits not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
proposals.sourceReason: 人神 names both human and spiritual aid. The existing English substitutes heaven alone and omits the human agents; the correction restores both without changing the hypothetical rhetorical question.
proposals.sourceChinese: 若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！
proposals.reason: 人神 names both human and spiritual aid. The existing English substitutes heaven alone and omits the human agents; the correction restores both without changing the hypothetical rhetorical question.

proposals.before: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his brothers ought to withdraw of their own accord.
proposals.after: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
proposals.sourceReason: 引領 means stretching the neck or looking up in expectation, not withdrawing from office. 自宜 does not supply a verb of retirement. The replacement leaves the object of expectation unstated, as in the Chinese.
proposals.sourceChinese: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
proposals.reason: 引領 means stretching the neck or looking up in expectation, not withdrawing from office. 自宜 does not supply a verb of retirement. The replacement leaves the object of expectation unstated, as in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to withdraw.
proposals.after: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.
proposals.sourceReason: The same 引領 error remains in the literal field: the Chinese expresses expectant looking, not withdrawal. The Weiyang kinship expression is retained without adding an unstated object of expectation.
proposals.sourceChinese: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
proposals.reason: The same 引領 error remains in the literal field: the Chinese expresses expectant looking, not withdrawal. The Weiyang kinship expression is retained without adding an unstated object of expectation.

proposals.before: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in frontier states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
proposals.after: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
proposals.sourceReason: 籓國 denotes the enfeoffed vassal states, not necessarily geographically frontier states. This is the repeated enfeoffment policy also expressed in s0256; only the unsupported frontier characterization is removed.
proposals.sourceChinese: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
proposals.reason: 籓國 denotes the enfeoffed vassal states, not necessarily geographically frontier states. This is the repeated enfeoffment policy also expressed in s0256; only the unsupported frontier characterization is removed.

proposals.before: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with frontier states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
proposals.after: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
proposals.sourceReason: The literal field repeats the unsupported geographical reading of 籓國 as frontier states. Vassal states preserves enfeoffment and agrees with the corrected use at s0256 without asserting location.
proposals.sourceChinese: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
proposals.reason: The literal field repeats the unsupported geographical reading of 籓國 as frontier states. Vassal states preserves enfeoffment and agrees with the corrected use at s0256 without asserting location.

proposals.before: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and name, are far apart in origin and position, and moreover are kin of the state; by reason one ought to yield and rejoice to suit the occasion.
proposals.after: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
proposals.sourceReason: The literal field still leaves the memorialist among the imperial kin, although 又國之戚昵 refers to Bing and his fellows in this contrast. It also treats 降悅 as rejoicing rather than deferential accommodation. The correction makes the kinship owner and the speaker who should defer explicit.
proposals.sourceChinese: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
proposals.reason: The literal field still leaves the memorialist among the imperial kin, although 又國之戚昵 refers to Bing and his fellows in this contrast. It also treats 降悅 as rejoicing rather than deferential accommodation. The correction makes the kinship owner and the speaker who should defer explicit.

proposals.before: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of column commanders and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.
proposals.after: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of generals and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.
proposals.sourceReason: 列將 occurs again here. Rendering it as column commanders repeats the unsupported office interpretation corrected at s0261 and in claim-440; generals preserves the military positions without importing a column-command title.
proposals.sourceChinese: 又與冰書曰：君以椒房之親，舅氏之昵，總據樞機，出內王命，兼擁列將州司之位，昆弟網羅，顯布畿甸。
proposals.reason: 列將 occurs again here. Rendering it as column commanders repeats the unsupported office interpretation corrected at s0261 and in claim-440; generals preserves the military positions without importing a column-command title.

proposals.before: Each time I read the histories, rulers never fail to pamper and indulge the maternal clan, letting them hold power and disorder the court; first they have glory beyond the age, then the burden of riding when unfit, the saying that love rightly becomes harm.
proposals.after: Whenever I read the histories, I see maternal relatives invariably pampered and indulged, allowed to hold power and disorder the court; first they enjoy glory surpassing their age, then incur the burden of riding when unfit; this is what is meant by love being sufficient to cause harm.
proposals.sourceReason: The literal field still makes rulers the explicit subject before the ambiguous they, obscuring the maternal relatives as recipients of glory and calamity. 愛之適足以為害 means love suffices to cause harm, not that love rightly becomes harm. Both substantive problems are corrected while retaining the 負乘 image.
proposals.sourceChinese: 每睹史傳，未嘗不寵恣母族，使執權亂朝，先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累，所謂愛之適足以為害。
proposals.reason: The literal field still makes rulers the explicit subject before the ambiguous they, obscuring the maternal relatives as recipients of glory and calamity. 愛之適足以為害 means love suffices to cause harm, not that love rightly becomes harm. Both substantive problems are corrected while retaining the 負乘 image.

proposals.before: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing the first sprout and ending favor; why not grant a single fief and let frontier states succeed one another, as Qi and Chen of Zhou?
proposals.after: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing incipient trouble and preserving favor to the end; why not establish them with a territorial fief and let the vassal states be inherited in succession, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?
proposals.sourceReason: 終寵 means sustaining favor to its end, not ending favor. 令籓國相承 concerns hereditary succession in the enfeoffed states, not frontier states replacing one another. These definite errors remain in the literal field despite correction of the en field.
proposals.sourceChinese: 吾常忿歷代之主，不盡防萌終寵之術，何不業以一土之封，令籓國相承，如周之齊、陳？
proposals.reason: 終寵 means sustaining favor to its end, not ending favor. 令籓國相承 concerns hereditary succession in the enfeoffed states, not frontier states replacing one another. These definite errors remain in the literal field despite correction of the en field.

proposals.before: Worthy men rallied to them; though eunuchs endangered them and the realm mourned, they could still walk without pride and gave their lives for the state.
proposals.after: Worthy men rallied to them; although eunuchs brought them into peril, the realm lamented them because they could nonetheless conduct themselves without arrogance and gave their lives for the state.
proposals.sourceReason: 故也 makes their unarrogant conduct and service at the cost of their lives the explanation for the realm lamenting them despite the eunuchs bringing them into peril. The existing wording loses this causal relation and reads 履 as physical walking.
proposals.sourceChinese: 賢士歸心，雖為閹豎所危，天下嗟痛，猶有能履以不驕，圖國亡身故也。
proposals.reason: 故也 makes their unarrogant conduct and service at the cost of their lives the explanation for the realm lamenting them despite the eunuchs bringing them into peril. The existing wording loses this causal relation and reads 履 as physical walking.

proposals.before: Worthy men gave them their hearts; though endangered by eunuch minions and mourned by the realm, they could still walk without pride and plotted for the state even at the cost of their lives.
proposals.after: Worthy men gave them their hearts; although they were endangered by eunuch minions, the realm lamented them, because they were still able to conduct themselves without arrogance and took thought for the state at the cost of their lives.
proposals.sourceReason: The literal field also omits the explanatory force of 故也 and turns conduct expressed by 履 into walking. The correction attaches the explanation to the realm lamenting them and retains the supplied Chinese without conjecturally replacing its unusual wording.
proposals.sourceChinese: 賢士歸心，雖為閹豎所危，天下嗟痛，猶有能履以不驕，圖國亡身故也。
proposals.reason: The literal field also omits the explanatory force of 故也 and turns conduct expressed by 履 into walking. The correction attaches the explanation to the realm lamenting them and retains the supplied Chinese without conjecturally replacing its unusual wording.

proposals.before: Bing seeing the memorial and letter was greatly afraid; because they were extremely distant, not what they could control; thereupon with He Chong and others memorialized to permit Huang to style King of Yan.
proposals.after: Bing, seeing the memorial and letter, was greatly afraid; because Huang was extremely far away and beyond his power to control, he thereupon, with He Chong and the others, memorialized to permit Huang to style himself King of Yan.
proposals.sourceReason: 其絕遠 refers to Huang, the distant person whom Bing cannot control, not to the memorial and letter or to a plural they. The correction restores the pronoun owner and the reflexive force of 皝稱燕王 without changing the event or introducing a date.
proposals.sourceChinese: 冰見表及書甚懼，以其絕遠，非所能制，遂與何充等奏聽皝稱燕王。
proposals.reason: 其絕遠 refers to Huang, the distant person whom Bing cannot control, not to the memorial and letter or to a plural they. The correction restores the pronoun owner and the reflexive force of 皝稱燕王 without changing the event or introducing a date.

sourceUnits.zh: 若親黨后族，必有傾辱之禍。
sourceUnits.en: when they favored kin and the empress's clan, overthrow and humiliation were sure to follow.
sourceUnits.literal: If they favored kin and the empress's clan, disaster of overthrow and humiliation was sure to follow.

sourceUnits.zh: 是以周之申伯號稱賢舅，以其身籓於外，不握朝權。
sourceUnits.en: Shen Bo of Zhou was praised as a worthy maternal uncle because he held a frontier fief and did not grasp court power.
sourceUnits.literal: Therefore Shen Bo of Zhou was called the worthy maternal uncle, because he was enfeoffed outside as a frontier lord and did not hold court power.

sourceUnits.zh: 降及秦昭，足為令主，委信二舅，幾至亂國。
sourceUnits.en: Even King Zhao of Qin, a capable ruler, trusted his two maternal uncles and nearly ruined the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Descending to King Zhao of Qin, who was enough to be called a fine ruler, he entrusted his two maternal uncles and nearly brought the state to disorder.

sourceUnits.zh: 逮于漢武，推重田蚡，萬機之要，無不決之。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Wu of Han elevated Tian Fen until every vital decision passed through him.
sourceUnits.literal: Reaching Emperor Wu of Han, who elevated Tian Fen, none of the myriad affairs' essentials went undecided by him.

sourceUnits.zh: 及蚡死後，切齒追恨。
sourceUnits.en: After Fen died, the emperor gnashed his teeth in bitter regret.
sourceUnits.literal: When Fen died, he gnashed his teeth in later regret.

sourceUnits.zh: 成帝暗弱，不能自立，內惑豔妻，外恣五舅，卒令王莽坐取帝位。
sourceUnits.en: Emperor Cheng was weak and could not stand alone; beguiled within by a beautiful consort and indulging the five maternal uncles without, he finally let Wang Mang seize the throne.
sourceUnits.literal: Emperor Cheng was dim and weak, unable to stand on his own; inwardly confused by a beautiful wife, outwardly indulging the five maternal uncles, he finally let Wang Mang sit and take the imperial throne.

sourceUnits.zh: 每覽斯事，孰不痛惋！
sourceUnits.en: Reading such cases, who does not feel pain and regret!
sourceUnits.literal: Each time one reads these affairs, who does not feel pain and regret!

sourceUnits.zh: 設使舅氏賢若穰侯、王鳳，則但聞有二臣，不聞有二主。
sourceUnits.en: If maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang or Wang Feng, one would hear of two ministers, not two rulers.
sourceUnits.literal: Suppose the maternal uncles were worthy like the Marquis of Rang and Wang Feng, then one would only hear of two ministers, not two lords.

sourceUnits.zh: 若其不才，則有竇憲、梁冀之禍。
sourceUnits.en: If they lacked talent, disasters like those of Dou Xian and Liang Ji followed.
sourceUnits.literal: If they lacked talent, there were the disasters of Dou Xian and Liang Ji.

sourceUnits.zh: 凡此成敗，亦既然矣。
sourceUnits.en: The lesson of these successes and failures is already plain.
sourceUnits.literal: All these successes and failures are already thus clear.

sourceUnits.zh: 苟能易軌，可無覆墜。
sourceUnits.en: Change course in time and collapse can be avoided.
sourceUnits.literal: If one could change course, one could avoid overturn and collapse.

sourceUnits.zh: 陛下命世天挺，當隆晉道，而遭國多難，殷憂備嬰，追述往事，至今楚灼。
sourceUnits.en: Your Majesty is heaven-born to exalt Jin's Way, yet the state has met repeated calamity; grief presses on every side, and recalling the past still burns.
sourceUnits.literal: Your Majesty is heaven-born to the age, destined to exalt Jin's Way, yet has encountered many hardships of state; deep grief presses on every side; recalling past affairs, to this day one burns with anguish.

sourceUnits.zh: 跡其所由，實因故司空亮居元舅之尊，勢業之重，執政裁下，輕侮邊將，故令蘇峻、祖約不勝其忿，遂致敗國。
sourceUnits.en: The root cause was the late Minister of Works Yu Liang: as chief maternal uncle he wielded overwhelming power, judged subordinates harshly, and insulted frontier generals until Su Jun and Zu Yue, unable to bear their rage, ruined the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Tracing where it came from, it was truly because the late Minister of Works Yu Liang occupied the honor of chief maternal uncle and the weight of power and achievement, governed and judged subordinates, and lightly insulted frontier generals, so that Su Jun and Zu Yue could not contain their rage and thus brought disaster on the state.

sourceUnits.zh: 至今太后發憤，一旦升遐。
sourceUnits.en: And now the Empress Dowager, overcome with indignation, has suddenly passed away.
sourceUnits.literal: Until now the Empress Dowager gave vent to her indignation and in one morning ascended to distant heaven.

sourceUnits.zh: 若社稷不靈，人神無助，豺狼之心當可極邪！
sourceUnits.en: Had the altars not been numinous and heaven not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
sourceUnits.literal: If the altars were not numinous and men and spirits gave no aid, would the heart of wolves and jackals be allowed to reach its limit!

sourceUnits.zh: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
sourceUnits.en: Past affairs are not forgotten, yet Yu Bing as directorate counselor and left general, with his brothers, inwardly holds the pivot and outwardly commands armies, unmatched among ministers.
sourceUnits.literal: Past affairs are not forgotten, the model for later affairs, yet Directorate Counselor and Left General Yu Bing and others inwardly hold the pivot, outwardly hold supreme command; brothers stand side by side, no minister has a peer.

sourceUnits.zh: 陛下深敦渭陽，冰等自宜引領。
sourceUnits.en: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his brothers ought to withdraw of their own accord.
sourceUnits.literal: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to withdraw.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣常謂世主若欲崇顯舅氏，何不封以籓國，豐其祿賜，限其勢利，使上無偏優，下無私論。
sourceUnits.en: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in frontier states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with frontier states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.

sourceUnits.zh: 如此，榮辱何從而生！
sourceUnits.en: Then whence would honor or disgrace arise!
sourceUnits.literal: Thus, from what would honor and disgrace arise!

sourceUnits.zh: 噂𠴲何辭而起！
sourceUnits.en: Whence would slander spring!
sourceUnits.literal: From what words would slander and calumny spring!

sourceUnits.zh: 往者惟亮一人，宿有名望，尚致世變，況今居之者素無聞焉！
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Yu Liang alone, though long renowned, still brought turmoil; how much more those who hold power today and were never heard of before!
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly there was only Yu Liang alone, long with a name of standing, yet still he brought change to the age; how much more those who hold the posts today, who from the first had no renown!

sourceUnits.zh: 且人情易惑，難以戶告，縱今陛下無私于彼，天下之人誰謂不私乎！
sourceUnits.en: Human feelings are easily swayed and cannot be told house to house; even if Your Majesty is impartial, who in the realm will believe it!
sourceUnits.literal: Moreover human feelings are easily confused and hard to tell door to door; even if Your Majesty today has no partiality toward them, who in the realm would say there is none!

sourceUnits.zh: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
sourceUnits.en: Bing and I differ in rank and station, yet as kin of the state I ought by rights to yield and rejoice at the occasion.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and name, are far apart in origin and position, and moreover are kin of the state; by reason one ought to yield and rejoice to suit the occasion.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣獨矯抗此言者，上為陛下，退為冰計，疾苟容之臣，坐鑒得失。
sourceUnits.en: I speak against the tide alone: for Your Majesty above and for Bing's sake below, hating ministers who only flatter and judging gain and loss plainly.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant alone presses this contrary speech: for Your Majesty above, for Bing's sake below; despising ministers who only accommodate; sitting in judgment of gain and loss.

sourceUnits.zh: 顛而不扶，焉用彼相！
sourceUnits.en: If one does not right what is overturned, of what use is that minister!
sourceUnits.literal: If one does not right what is overturned, what use is that minister!

sourceUnits.zh: 昔徐福陳霍氏之戒，宣帝不從，至令忠臣更為逆族，良由察之不審，防之無漸。
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Xu Fu warned against the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not heed him, and loyal ministers became a traitorous house because he did not examine carefully or guard against gradual encroachment.
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly Xu Fu set forth the warning of the Huo clan; Emperor Xuan did not follow it, so that even loyal ministers became a rebellious lineage, truly because investigation was not careful and prevention had no gradual steps.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣今所陳，可謂防漸矣。
sourceUnits.en: What I now set forth is prevention at the first sign.
sourceUnits.literal: What your servant now sets forth may be called prevention at the first sign.

sourceUnits.zh: 但恐陛下不明臣之忠，不用臣之計，事過之日，更處焦爛之後耳。
sourceUnits.en: I fear only that Your Majesty may not see my loyalty or use my plan, and that after disaster passes you will again stand amid the ashes.
sourceUnits.literal: Only fearing that Your Majesty may not understand your servant's loyalty and may not use your servant's plan; after the affair has passed, one will again be in the charred wreckage.

sourceUnits.zh: 昔王章、劉向每上封事，未嘗不指斥王氏，故令二子或死或刑。
sourceUnits.en: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang denounced the Wang clan in every sealed memorial and ended dead or punished.
sourceUnits.literal: Formerly Wang Zhang and Liu Xiang, each time they submitted sealed memorials, never failed to denounce the Wang clan, so both men ended dead or under punishment.

sourceUnits.zh: 谷永、張禹依違不對，故容身苟免，取譏於世。
sourceUnits.en: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and preserved themselves, winning only the age's ridicule.
sourceUnits.literal: Gu Yong and Zhang Yu equivocated and did not answer directly, so they preserved themselves and escaped, drawing ridicule from the age.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣被髮殊俗，位為上將，夙夜惟憂，罔知所報，惟當外殄寇仇，內盡忠規，陳力輸誠，以答國恩。
sourceUnits.en: I wear disheveled hair in a foreign land, hold supreme command, worry day and night how to repay the state, and can only destroy enemies abroad and offer loyal remonstrance within.
sourceUnits.literal: Your servant wears disheveled hair in a foreign land, holds the rank of supreme general, worries day and night and knows not how to repay, and can only destroy enemies abroad, exhaust loyal remonstrance within, exert strength and offer sincerity to answer the state's grace.

sourceUnits.zh: 臣若不言，誰當言者！
sourceUnits.en: If I do not speak, who will!
sourceUnits.literal: If your servant does not speak, who will speak!

sourceUnits.zh: 又與冰書曰：君以椒房之親，舅氏之昵，總據樞機，出內王命，兼擁列將州司之位，昆弟網羅，顯布畿甸。
sourceUnits.en: He also wrote to Yu Bing: By empress kinship and maternal closeness you hold the pivot, issue and receive royal commands, and with your brothers hold command and provincial posts, your network displayed across the capital region.
sourceUnits.literal: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of column commanders and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.

sourceUnits.zh: 自秦、漢以來，隆赫之極，豈有若此者乎！
sourceUnits.en: Since Qin and Han, has splendor reached such a height!
sourceUnits.literal: Since Qin and Han, has there been such extreme splendor!

sourceUnits.zh: 以吾觀之，若功就事舉，必享申伯之名；
sourceUnits.en: In my view, if your work succeeds you will enjoy Shen Bo's fame;
sourceUnits.literal: In my view, if merit is achieved and affairs succeed, you will surely enjoy the name of Shen Bo;

sourceUnits.zh: 如或不立，將不免梁竇之跡矣。
sourceUnits.en: if not, you will not escape the fate of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.
sourceUnits.literal: If not, you will not escape the track of Liang Ji and Dou Xian.

sourceUnits.zh: 每睹史傳，未嘗不寵恣母族，使執權亂朝，先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累，所謂愛之適足以為害。
sourceUnits.en: History shows that rulers who pamper the maternal clan and let them rule always win brief glory and then the ruin of "love becomes harm."
sourceUnits.literal: Each time I read the histories, rulers never fail to pamper and indulge the maternal clan, letting them hold power and disorder the court; first they have glory beyond the age, then the burden of riding when unfit, the saying that love rightly becomes harm.

sourceUnits.zh: 吾常忿歷代之主，不盡防萌終寵之術，何不業以一土之封，令籓國相承，如周之齊、陳？
sourceUnits.en: I resent that successive rulers never fully guarded against early favor; why not grant a single fief and let frontier states succeed one another, as Qi and Chen of Zhou?
sourceUnits.literal: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing the first sprout and ending favor; why not grant a single fief and let frontier states succeed one another, as Qi and Chen of Zhou?

sourceUnits.zh: 如此則永保南面之尊，復何黜辱之憂乎！
sourceUnits.en: Then they would forever preserve honor facing south, with no fear of dismissal or disgrace!
sourceUnits.literal: Then they would forever preserve the honor of facing south; what worry of dismissal and disgrace!

sourceUnits.zh: 竇武、何進好善虛己。
sourceUnits.en: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and humbled themselves.
sourceUnits.literal: Dou Wu and He Jin loved goodness and emptied themselves.

sourceUnits.zh: 賢士歸心，雖為閹豎所危，天下嗟痛，猶有能履以不驕，圖國亡身故也。
sourceUnits.en: Worthy men rallied to them; though eunuchs endangered them and the realm mourned, they could still walk without pride and gave their lives for the state.
sourceUnits.literal: Worthy men gave them their hearts; though endangered by eunuch minions and mourned by the realm, they could still walk without pride and plotted for the state even at the cost of their lives.

sourceUnits.zh: 方今四海有倒懸之急，中夏逋僭逆之寇，家有漉血之怨，人有復仇之憾，甯得安枕逍遙，雅談卒歲邪！
sourceUnits.en: Now the realm hangs inverted, rebels roam China, families bear blood-soaked grievances and men thirst for vengeance; how can one rest at ease and talk elegantly through the year!
sourceUnits.literal: Now the four seas have the urgency of the inverted hanging; within China flee usurping rebels; families bear blood-soaked grievances and men the regret of vengeance; how can one rest on pillows at ease, discoursing elegantly through the year!

sourceUnits.zh: 吾雖寡德，過蒙先帝列將之授，以數郡之人，尚欲併吞強虜，是以自頃迄今，交鋒接刃，一時務農，三時用武，而猶師徒不頓，倉有餘粟，敵人日畏，我境日廣，況乃王者之威，堂堂之勢，豈可同年而語哉！
sourceUnits.en: I am little in virtue, yet the former emperor made me a column commander; with several commanderies I still mean to swallow strong foes. From lately until now I farm one season and fight three, yet my armies do not fail, my granaries hold surplus, the enemy daily fears us and our borders widen daily; how much more the majesty of a king and stately power, how can these be compared!
sourceUnits.literal: Though I am few in virtue, I have unduly received the former emperor's grant of command over the columns; with the people of several commanderies I still wish to swallow strong enemies; therefore from recently until now, clashing blades and meeting swords, one season for farming and three for war, yet the army is not exhausted, the granaries have surplus grain, the enemy daily fears us and our borders daily widen; how much more the king's majesty and stately power, how can they be spoken of in the same year!

sourceUnits.zh: 冰見表及書甚懼，以其絕遠，非所能制，遂與何充等奏聽皝稱燕王。
sourceUnits.en: On seeing the memorial and the letter, Yu Bing was greatly alarmed; because Huang was so far away and beyond his power to control, he joined He Chong and others in memorializing that Huang be allowed to style himself King of Yan.
sourceUnits.literal: Bing seeing the memorial and letter was greatly afraid; because they were extremely distant, not what they could control; thereupon with He Chong and others memorialized to permit Huang to style King of Yan.

EnglishProposals.before: Bing and I differ in rank and station, yet as kin of the state I ought by rights to yield and rejoice at the occasion.
EnglishProposals.after: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
EnglishProposals.sourceChinese: 臣與冰等名位殊班，出處懸邈，又國之戚昵，理應降悅，以適事會。
EnglishProposals.sourceReason: 又國之戚昵 refers to Bing and the other imperial maternal relatives, not Huang as the supplied English explicitly claims. The contrast explains why Huang would ordinarily defer despite his contrary remonstrance.
EnglishProposals.reason: 又國之戚昵 refers to Bing and the other imperial maternal relatives, not Huang as the supplied English explicitly claims. The contrast explains why Huang would ordinarily defer despite his contrary remonstrance.

EnglishProposals.before: History shows that rulers who pamper the maternal clan and let them rule always win brief glory and then the ruin of "love becomes harm."
EnglishProposals.after: Reading the histories, I see maternal relatives indulged and allowed to wield power and disorder the court: first they enjoy extraordinary glory, then suffer the consequences of holding positions beyond their station. This is what is meant by love proving sufficient to cause harm.
EnglishProposals.sourceChinese: 每睹史傳，未嘗不寵恣母族，使執權亂朝，先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累，所謂愛之適足以為害。
EnglishProposals.sourceReason: 先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累 concerns the favored maternal clan rather than rulers winning glory. 殊世 does not mean brief; 負乘 alludes to occupying an unsuitable elevated position.
EnglishProposals.reason: 先有殊世之榮，尋有負乘之累 concerns the favored maternal clan rather than rulers winning glory. 殊世 does not mean brief; 負乘 alludes to occupying an unsuitable elevated position.

EnglishProposals.before: I resent that successive rulers never fully guarded against early favor; why not grant a single fief and let frontier states succeed one another, as Qi and Chen of Zhou?
EnglishProposals.after: I have often resented that successive rulers did not fully master the means of preventing incipient trouble while preserving favor to the end. Why not establish these relatives with a territorial fief and let their descendants inherit the vassal state, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?
EnglishProposals.sourceChinese: 吾常忿歷代之主，不盡防萌終寵之術，何不業以一土之封，令籓國相承，如周之齊、陳？
EnglishProposals.sourceReason: 令籓國相承 describes hereditary succession in the enfeoffed states, not frontier states succeeding one another. 防萌終寵 distinguishes preventing budding trouble from sustaining favor, rather than guarding against early favor.
EnglishProposals.reason: 令籓國相承 describes hereditary succession in the enfeoffed states, not frontier states succeeding one another. 防萌終寵 distinguishes preventing budding trouble from sustaining favor, rather than guarding against early favor.

EnglishProposals.before: I am little in virtue, yet the former emperor made me a column commander; with several commanderies I still mean to swallow strong foes. From lately until now I farm one season and fight three, yet my armies do not fail, my granaries hold surplus, the enemy daily fears us and our borders widen daily; how much more the majesty of a king and stately power, how can these be compared!
EnglishProposals.after: Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received appointment as one of the former emperor’s generals. With the people of only several commanderies, I still aspire to engulf powerful enemies. Thus, from recent times until now we have crossed weapons in battle, farming for one season and fighting for three; yet our troops are not exhausted, our granaries have surplus grain, our enemies fear us more each day, and our territory grows daily. How much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!
EnglishProposals.sourceChinese: 吾雖寡德，過蒙先帝列將之授，以數郡之人，尚欲併吞強虜，是以自頃迄今，交鋒接刃，一時務農，三時用武，而猶師徒不頓，倉有餘粟，敵人日畏，我境日廣，況乃王者之威，堂堂之勢，豈可同年而語哉！
EnglishProposals.sourceReason: 以數郡之人 includes the people of the commanderies; 交鋒接刃 is omitted. 列將 need not denote a formal column-commander office. 王者 contrasts Huang’s limited resources with imperial sovereign power, not Huang’s own royal title.

EnglishProposals.sourceReason: 同年而語 is an idiom of comparison, not a same-year assertion; 列將 does not literally mean command over columns. The supplied literal rendering must not be used as chronological evidence.

EnglishProposals.before: Past affairs are not forgotten, yet Yu Bing as directorate counselor and left general, with his brothers, inwardly holds the pivot and outwardly commands armies, unmatched among ministers.
EnglishProposals.after: Remembering past events provides a guide for the future. Yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows control the central levers of government within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side in office, with no other ministers to match them.
EnglishProposals.sourceChinese: 前事不忘，後事之表，而中書監、左將軍冰等內執樞機，外擁上將，昆弟並列，人臣莫疇。
EnglishProposals.reason: The idiomatic field drops 後事之表. Both fields misrender 中書監 as Directorate Counselor; retain both named offices, the inside/outside contrast, simultaneous brothers and unmatched ministerial power. No date or identity is inferred.

EnglishProposals.before: Past affairs are not forgotten, the model for later affairs, yet Directorate Counselor and Left General Yu Bing and others inwardly hold the pivot, outwardly hold supreme command; brothers stand side by side, no minister has a peer.
EnglishProposals.after: Past events, if not forgotten, are a model for later affairs; yet Yu Bing, Director of the Secretariat and General of the Left, and his fellows grasp the pivot within and hold senior military commands outside; the brothers stand side by side, with no other minister to match them.
